🎙
Remarks and answers to media questions
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov following the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
(Atlanta, October 30, 2026)
❓
Question: Have your contacts with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio taken place, or are they planned? Since we are in the United States, does the resumption of direct air links with the country remain on the agenda? Are there prospects for resolving the issue regarding our diplomatic property?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
We had a productive conversation, albeit a short one – for understandable reasons – because, as our host, he has many duties that do not allow him to spend much time on contacts outside the G20 framework.
Nevertheless, the engagement did take place. We discussed both certain aspects of our bilateral relations and interaction at multilateral venues, including the
#UN
, the
#G20
and
#APEC
, whose summit will be held very soon, in November, in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.
I have said on numerous occasions that the Americans observe the rules of classical diplomacy, regardless of the tensions in our relations. There have always been – and there always will be – problems between Russia and the United States. Moreover, as US Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
himself acknowledged at our
first meeting
in February 2025 in Riyadh, in the overwhelming majority of cases our national interests – America’s and Russia’s – will not coincide.
However, when those interests do align,
it would be foolish and wrong not to translate that alignment into the execution of joint, mutually beneficial projects
. Conversely, when the interests of Russia and the United States do not coincide, it would be a crime to allow that divergence to escalate into an open clash, or indeed into any confrontation at all.
Therefore – despite all our differences – the readiness and interest of the Americans in dialogue at the most varied levels, including between the presidents, the foreign ministers and a whole host of other channels, can, of course,
only be welcomed.
This serves as a good lesson for our European colleagues, who continue to adopt a position of what one might call an
arrogant boycott
. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, who asked for a
meeting
with me in New York a month ago, issued a statement yesterday or this morning to the effect that he would tell Sergey Lavrov everything about the
“aggressive war”
and would never be photographed with him.
I call this “family photo diplomacy”.
If the main concern for them is how they look in the group portrait and who is standing next to them, then
that says it all.

item.title: 🇷🇺 Russia–South Africa Strengthen Cooperation on Consumer Protection On 29 October, on the sidelines of the
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇿🇦 Russia–South Africa Strengthen Cooperation on Consumer Protection On 29 October, on the sidelines of the Third Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow, Head of Rospotrebnadzor Anna Popova and Acting Commissioner of South Africa’s National Consumer Commission Hardin Ratshisusu signed a Memorandum of Cooperation. The agreement provides for closer institutional ties, the exchange of expertise and information, and the development of joint approaches to protecting consumer rights, including within the #BRICS framework. The Memorandum represents a practical step towards translating dialogue into concrete cooperation. ❗️ Russia remains committed to sharing its extensive experience, knowledge and best practices with African countries , supporting the development of effective consumer protection systems and strengthening partnerships based on mutual respect, trust and the exchange of expertise. 📸 Photo: Rospotrebnadzor #RussiaSouthAfrica #RussiaWithAfrica

✍️
Article
by Ambassador of Russia to Indonesia
Sergei Tolchenov
, “
The Arctic: From the Northern Sea Route to Greater Eurasia”
, published in
The Jakarta Post
(October 29, 2026)
.
Key points:
• The
Arctic
holds a
special place
in Russia’s domestic and foreign policy. Maintaining
peace and stability
in the region, reducing national security threats and creating favorable external conditions for Russia’s socioeconomic development are among the key priorities outlined in the
Concept of the Foreign Policy of the Russian Federation
.
•
The Northern Sea Route
(NSR)
is central to the development of the Arctic.
It is the shortest maritime route connecting the European part of Russia with the Russian Far East, running through the Arctic Ocean and, in part, the Pacific Ocean. Amid growing geopolitical uncertainty, the NSR is becoming an increasingly attractive alternative to traditional southern shipping routes. Its advantages include
shorter distances, lower environmental impact and the economic benefits
of reduced transit times, as well as
greater security.
Developing the full potential of the
Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor,
of which the NSR is a key component, is therefore becoming a major priority for Russia’s cooperation with international partners in the Arctic.
• The waters along the Northern Sea Route are free from piracy, armed conflict, military confrontation and territorial disputes.
Russia’s
efforts have played a significant role in preserving this situation, guided by the principle that the Arctic should remain a
region of peace and cooperation.
On the other hand,
Western countries
have increasingly treated the Arctic as an
arena of geopolitical competition
and sought to establish military superiority in the region. NATO continues to expand its military activities in the High North, including through operation Arctic Sentry, launched in February, 2026, to strengthen the Alliance’s military presence at high latitudes.
• Russia maintains close cooperation with
China
and
India
on Arctic issues. There are also promising opportunities to strengthen ties with other
BRICS
members, including
Indonesia.
In April 2025, for example, the
Far East and Arctic Development Corporation
(KRDV) and the
Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry
(Kadin) signed a cooperation agreement in Jakarta. It opened opportunities for expanding bilateral investment cooperation, enabling interested businesses to participate in joint sector-specific events and facilitating targeted business missions. KRDV representatives visited the
Science and Technology Park of the University of Indonesia
to discuss joint projects involving Russian and Indonesian research institutions and industrial companies in support of the development of Russia’s Far East and the Arctic Zone. Our countries are also deepening their cooperation in science and education. Links have been established between
Gadjah Mada University
(UGM) and Russia’s
Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute.
• Studying the Arctic is of strategic importance to Indonesia, particularly in understanding and anticipating the effects of global climate change. Conditions in the Arctic have significant implications for the
environmental resilience of tropical countries and global sea levels
, while developments in the region also carry wider
geopolitical and economic significance,
particularly with the opening of new maritime routes.
•
Russia
is working to establish
standards for responsible Arctic governance and sustainable socioeconomic development,
while
safeguarding the region’s natural resources and the cultural heritage
of its indigenous peoples. It continues to promote the
Arctic as an integral part of a broader Eurasian space of security and cooperation.
As a key component of the Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor, the Northern Sea Route is expected to play an important role in advancing Russia’s President Vladimir Putin’s flagship initiative to form the
Greater Eurasian Partnership.

item.description: 🎙 Opening remarks by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with President of Eritrea Isaias Afwerki on the sidelines of the Third Russia–Africa Summit (Moscow, October 30, 2026) 💬 Vladimir Putin : Let me begin by thanking you for taking part in the #RussiaAfrica Summit . Thanks in part to your participation, I believe we have achieved good results . Today, we have an opportunity to discuss our bilateral relations, as Russian-Eritrean relations are progressing . ☝️ We must , of course, pay greater attention to trade and economic cooperation and discuss measures to increase bilateral trade. We see promising opportunities in energy, mining, infrastructure, agriculture and fisheries . We are helping to strengthen your food security. 🇷🇺 🇪🇷 Russia and Eritrea share common positions on many pressing international issues . Mr President, we are, of course, grateful to you for supporting Russian initiatives at the UN and other multilateral platforms. We see this and, I would like to stress, fully appreciate it. We have already worked productively together during the Summit . Once again, we are pleased to have this opportunity to discuss our bilateral ties and their further development . #RussiaEritrea

🎙
Remarks and answers to media questions
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov following the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
(Atlanta, October 30, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
We support
the US Presidency’s
firm commitment to
depoliticising discussions
and focusing on the issues originally agreed upon as the
#G20
’s agenda.
This year’s meeting is, of course,
part of the preparations for
the Miami Summit
, which will take place in December.
The main topics were
the impact of geopolitics on economic processes
(an important issue),
energy
,
food and supply chains
– in other words, everything affected by unlawful sanctions and Western policies.
To our American hosts’ credit, they
do not shy away
from discussing these matters and
listen attentively
. I do not know to what extent this will be reflected in the final agreed documents, but the approach is right:
☝️
depoliticise discussions and focus on real problems
.
Another point that US Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
particularly emphasised when discussing preparations for the Miami Summit was that
twenty countries, the European Union and the African Union
are represented here. Given the influence of
#G20
members on the global economy and their combined economic weight, however,
the decisions we take will affect virtually every country
. We must always bear this in mind.
🤝
Let me reiterate that we welcome this firm commitment to dialogue
.
Work on
the Miami Summit’s outcome documents
has, in fact, already begun.
There will be many difficult issues
, since interests are at stake across all these areas, including energy and food security. The impact of conflicts, including
the war unleashed against us by the West through the Ukrainian regime
, remains to be discussed. <...>
***
Other key points
:
• Under the pragmatic
US Presidency
of the
#G20
, we believe
there is a chance of reaching agreements that will be implemented
.
•
We see no need to add another European voice
[Poland]
to the G20
, especially one that is
far from constructive
. You know the positions Poland regularly voices at international events. The G20 must reflect actual trends in the global economy, where
countries of the Global South and East
are gaining prominence.
• We spoke [with US Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
] about
certain aspects of our bilateral relations
and cooperation in multilateral forums, including the
#UN
, the
#G20
and
#APEC
, that
will host a Summit shortly
in Shenzhen (China).
• Despite all our differences,
the US willingness and interest in pursuing dialogue
at various levels and through a range of other channels
can only be welcomed
. This is a good lesson for our European colleagues, who persist in their
arrogant boycott
.
• Everyone can see that
the Europeans
want to squeeze their way
into the negotiating process
[on Ukraine]. Clearly, they want to avoid leaving these negotiations solely to Russia and the US at all costs. What matters is not what the Europeans want, but
what added value they can actually bring
.
• As for the talks in Abu Dhabi, I can say that
they will take place
. Our position is well known.
It is unclear
, however, what the Ukrainians intend to bring to the negotiating table.
👉
As President Vladimir Putin has said
, if Zelensky wants a meeting,
he can come to Moscow
. We guarantee his safety and security, which, as far as I understand,
cannot be guaranteed in Kiev
.
